description: Na₄GeSe₄ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pnma space group. There are five inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Se²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaSe₆ octahedra that share corners with four GeSe₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids, edges with six NaSe₅ square pyramids,  an edgeedge with one GeSe₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 3.02-3.23 Å. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to five Se²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaSe₅ square pyramids that share corners with four equivalent NaSe₅ square pyramids, corners with three equivalent GeSe₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids, edges with two equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra,  an edgeedge with one GeSe₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids. There are three shorter (2.99 Å) and two longer (3.25 Å) Na-Se bond lengths. In the third Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five Se²⁻ atoms. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.93-3.36 Å. In the fourth Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to four Se²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one NaSe₆ octahedra, corners with five NaSe₅ square pyramids, corners with two equivalent GeSe₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one NaSe₆ octahedra,  an edgeedge with one NaSe₅ square pyramid,  an edgeedge with one GeSe₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaSe₄ trigonal pyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 24°. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.91-2.97 Å. In the fifth Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to five Se²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaSe₅ square pyramids that share corners with three NaSe₅ square pyramids,  a cornercorner with one GeSe₄ tetrahedra, corners with four equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids, edges with two equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra,  an edgeedge with one NaSe₅ square pyramid, and edges with two GeSe₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.94-3.43 Å. There are two inequivalent Ge⁴⁺ sites. In the first Ge⁴⁺ site, Ge⁴⁺ is bonded to four Se²⁻ atoms to form GeSe₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent NaSe₅ square pyramids, and edges with three NaSe₅ square pyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 9-66°. There are a spread of Ge-Se bond distances ranging from 2.38-2.41 Å. In the second Ge⁴⁺ site, Ge⁴⁺ is bonded to four Se²⁻ atoms to form GeSe₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaSe₆ octahedra, corners with three equivalent NaSe₅ square pyramids, corners with four equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one NaSe₆ octahedra, edges with two equivalent NaSe₅ square pyramids, and edges with two equivalent NaSe₄ trigonal pyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 1°. There are a spread of Ge-Se bond distances ranging from 2.38-2.40 Å. There are six inequivalent Se²⁻ sites. In the first Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form distorted SeNa₅Ge octahedra that share corners with five SeNa₅Ge octahedra,  a cornercorner with one SeNa₄Ge trigonal bipyramid, and edges with five SeNa₅Ge octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 17-59°. In the second Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to seven Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom. In the third Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to four Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing SeNa₄Ge trigonal bipyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 12-81°. In the fourth Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form distorted SeNa₅Ge octahedra that share corners with six SeNa₅Ge octahedra, corners with two equivalent SeNa₄Ge trigonal bipyramids, edges with three SeNa₅Ge octahedra, and  an edgeedge with one SeNa₄Ge trigonal bipyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 17-57°. In the fifth Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded in a distorted see-saw-like geometry to three Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom. In the sixth Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form SeNa₅Ge octahedra that share corners with two equivalent SeNa₅Ge octahedra, corners with two equivalent SeNa₄Ge trigonal bipyramids, and edges with six SeNa₅Ge octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 29°.
